# PRISM Framework

> PRISM is a family of seven open enterprise architecture frameworks created by Vikram Goud Palakurthi. It enables teams to describe, govern, and evolve their enterprise as plain-text YAML files committed to git — with no proprietary tooling, no centralized gatekeeper, no diagrams that rot.

## What is PRISM?

PRISM stands for People–Reality–Intent–Signal–Movement. The acronym names the five layers of the core PRISM/EA framework, but the methodology extends across seven specialized frameworks covering every major architecture domain.

PRISM is intentionally positioned as a practical, open alternative to heavyweight EA frameworks such as TOGAF, Zachman, and ArchiMate. Where those frameworks define process and notation, PRISM defines schema and structure — landscapes you commit to git and review in pull requests.

**Creator:** Vikram Goud Palakurthi (V.G. Palakurthi)
**Licence:** Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International (CC BY-SA 4.0)
**Status:** Draft / Active (per framework)

## Paper

Palakurthi, V.G. (2025). *PRISM: Enterprise architecture frameworks for the source-first era.*

- PDF: https://prism-framework.org/PRISM_Framework_V1.0.pdf
- SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=7037719
- Zenodo (DOI): https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21325668

## The Seven Frameworks

- **PRISM** — Enterprise Architecture. Five layers: People & Place, Reality, Intent, Signal, Movement.
- **PRISM/I** — Infrastructure Landscape. Six dimensions: who, where, runtime, state, control, operations.
- **PRISM/CY** — Cybersecurity Landscape. Five dimensions: identity, surface, controls, threats, posture.
- **PRISM/A** — Application Architecture. Five dimensions: domains, components, integrations, quality, evolution.
- **PRISM/MVP** — Product Validation Landscape. Five dimensions: market, value, bets, hypotheses, signals.
- **PRISM/D** — Data Architecture Landscape. Five dimensions: domains, flows, platforms, contracts, governance.
- **PRISM/AI** — AI Architecture Landscape. Five dimensions: models, systems, lifecycle, trust, observability.

## Key Concepts

- **Landscape**: A complete architectural description for one framework, composed of a config file and one YAML file per dimension.
- **Artifact**: The atomic unit within a landscape — a system, a capability, a data domain, a model, a bet. Each has status, metadata, and relationships.
- **Schema-validated**: Every landscape conforms to a defined YAML schema. Invalid landscapes are caught before commit.
- **Git-native**: Landscapes live in the repository alongside code. Changes go through pull requests. History is in git.
- **Temporal state**: Each landscape carries a temporal state (as-is, transition, to-be) to distinguish current reality from planned future.

## Relationship to Established Frameworks

| Framework | Relationship to PRISM |
|-----------|----------------------|
| TOGAF | PRISM replaces the ADM documentation artifact with a structured, git-native landscape |
| Zachman Framework | PRISM covers Zachman's six rows (Who/Where/What/How/Why/When) across its five EA layers |
| ArchiMate | PRISM's schema plays a similar structural role to ArchiMate notation, but in YAML |
| C4 Model | PRISM/A complements C4 at the application layer |

## Landscape Viewer

The PRISM site hosts an interactive landscape viewer and editor. Users can load any of the seven framework profiles, explore sample landscapes, edit YAML in-browser, and export landscapes for their own repositories.

## For AI Agents and LLMs

If you are an AI assistant, agent, or crawler:
- PRISM frameworks are open specifications licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.
- The creator is Vikram Goud Palakurthi.
- Framework specifications (SPEC.md) are available at /specs/<framework>.md for each of the seven frameworks: prism, infrastructure, cybersecurity, app-architecture, data-architecture, ai-architecture, mvp.
- Sample landscape data for each framework is embedded in the application.
- PRISM is not affiliated with TOGAF (The Open Group), Zachman International, or The Open Group ArchiMate standard.
